subject: Literacy
title: Loud, quiet and my voice
objectives: Children will make a loud and a quiet sound on request.
Children will use their voices in play, such as a whisper and a shout.
content: Making loud and quiet sounds, using the voice for whispering, shouting and humming, and high and low voices.
teachingActivities: Show loud with big arms and quiet with a finger to the lips; model each voice before children try; praise every attempt and keep shouting short.
learnerActivities: Make loud and quiet sounds on request, whisper and shout, and copy high and low voices.
resources: Picture cards of a lion and a mouse
assessment: Observe whether each child changes the loudness of a sound on request and joins in voice play.
expectedOutcomes: Changes the loudness of their voice on request.
Uses a voice sound to join a game.
crossCurricular: Social Habits: indoor and outdoor voices

lessons.title: Loud and quiet drum
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will make a loud and a quiet sound with a drum on request.
successCriteria: Plays the drum loudly when asked
Plays the drum quietly when asked
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stop and listen for a few seconds and point to the source of a familiar sound.
resources: A drum stick or a soft mallet
Picture cards of a lion and a mouse
lessons.starter: Beat the drum loudly and say "Loud! Boom, boom." Then tap it softly and whisper "Quiet. Tap, tap."
teacherActivities: Show the lion card and play a loud beat. Show the mouse card and play a quiet beat. Say the words loud and quiet.
Play loud or quiet and ask "Is it loud or quiet?"
Let each child play the drum when you hold up the lion or mouse card.
Play a short pattern: loud, quiet, loud, quiet.
learnerActivities: Children listen and open their arms wide for loud and put a finger to the lips for quiet.
Children answer with actions or words.
Child plays loud for the lion and quiet for the mouse.
Children copy the actions.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the lion card and play a loud beat. Show the mouse card and play a quiet beat. Say the words loud and quiet. Children: Children listen and open their arms wide for loud and put a finger to the lips for quiet.
Step 2. Teacher: Play loud or quiet and ask "Is it loud or quiet?" Children: Children answer with actions or words.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child play the drum when you hold up the lion or mouse card. Children: Child plays loud for the lion and quiet for the mouse.
Step 4. Teacher: Play a short pattern: loud, quiet, loud, quiet. Children: Children copy the actions.

practical.title: Lion and mouse drum
steps: Sit in a circle with the drum in the middle.
Hold up the lion or mouse card.
Each child takes a turn to play loud or quiet to match the card.
practical.safety: Use a soft mallet and keep the drum away from the children’s ears. Stop if a child covers their ears.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand to play and say "loud" or "quiet" with them.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose a card and play for the group to guess.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the lion loud or quiet?
Can you make a quiet sound?

expectedOutcomes: Plays a loud and a quiet sound on request
Shows loud or quiet with an action
lessons.conclusion: Play a very quiet tap and a loud boom and say "Loud and quiet."
lessons.homeConnection: At home, bang a pot loudly and tap it quietly and say loud and quiet.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "make a loud and a quiet sound with a drum on request" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Loud like a lion, boom, boom, boom. Quiet like a mouse, tap, tap, tap.

lessons.title: Whisper and shout
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will whisper and say a word loudly on request.
successCriteria: Says a word loudly when asked
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stop and listen for a few seconds and point to the source of a familiar sound.
lessons.starter: Hold up the puppet and whisper "Hello" in its ear. Then say "Hello!" in a big voice.
teacherActivities: Make the puppet whisper "Hello" and then say "HELLO!" Say "Whisper" and "big voice".
Whisper a word such as "baby" and ask the children to whisper it back.
Say a word in a big voice and ask the children to say it loudly, once only.
Let each child talk to the puppet in a whisper or a big voice.
learnerActivities: Children watch and copy the puppet’s voices.
Children whisper the word.
Children say the word in a big voice.
Child chooses a voice and says hello.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Make the puppet whisper "Hello" and then say "HELLO!" Say "Whisper" and "big voice". Children: Children watch and copy the puppet’s voices.
Step 2. Teacher: Whisper a word such as "baby" and ask the children to whisper it back. Children: Children whisper the word.
Step 3. Teacher: Say a word in a big voice and ask the children to say it loudly, once only. Children: Children say the word in a big voice.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child talk to the puppet in a whisper or a big voice. Children: Child chooses a voice and says hello.

practical.title: Telephone talk
steps: Give a toy telephone to a pair of children.
One whispers hello and the other whispers back.
Change voice to a big voice and swap pairs.
practical.safety: Keep big voices short so no child strains their voice. Use a clean toy telephone and wipe it between turns.

differentiation.support: Whisper with the child and use a gesture for the big voice.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose a word to whisper and then shout to the puppet.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you whisper?
questions.expected: Child whispers a sound or word.

expectedOutcomes: Uses a big voice briefly on request
lessons.homeConnection: At home, whisper a word to your child and ask them to whisper it back, then try a big voice.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "whisper and say a word loudly on request" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Voices in play
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will use their voices to join in a play game.
successCriteria: Makes a voice sound in a game
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stop and listen for a few seconds and point to the source of a familiar sound.
lessons.starter: Push the toy car and say "Brum, brum." Ask the children "What does the car say?"
teacherActivities: Drive the car along the mat saying "Brum, brum". Then show the aeroplane and say "Nee-ow."
Show the cat and say "Meow." Ask "What does the cat say?"
Move each toy and wait for the children to make its sound before it moves.
Let each child choose a toy and make its sound.
learnerActivities: Children copy the voice sounds.
Children say "meow".
Children make the sound to make the toy go.
Child moves the toy and makes the sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Drive the car along the mat saying "Brum, brum". Then show the aeroplane and say "Nee-ow." Children: Children copy the voice sounds.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the cat and say "Meow." Ask "What does the cat say?" Children: Children say "meow".
Step 3. Teacher: Move each toy and wait for the children to make its sound before it moves. Children: Children make the sound to make the toy go.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a toy and make its sound. Children: Child moves the toy and makes the sound.

practical.title: Voice toys
steps: Place three toys on a mat.
Each child picks a toy and moves it while making its sound.
practical.safety: Keep the toys large with no loose parts. Supervise closely and keep the floor clear of small items.

differentiation.support: Move the toy together and make the sound with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a sound for a toy and ask a friend to guess.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you make the cat sound?

expectedOutcomes: Makes a voice sound in play
Waits for the toy to move
lessons.conclusion: Park the toys in a box and say "Night, night car. Night, night cat."
lessons.homeConnection: Play with a toy car or a cup at home and make a sound for each move.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use their voices to join in a play game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: High and low voices
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Children will copy a high voice and a low voice.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stop and listen for a few seconds and point to the source of a familiar sound.
lessons.starter: Make the mouse puppet squeak in a high voice and the bear puppet growl in a low voice. Ask "Who is it?"
teacherActivities: Show the mouse and squeak up high with a hand raised. Show the bear and growl low with a hand lowered.
Say "High or low?" and make a sound.
Sing "ooh" going up and down with the scarf.
Give each child a turn to be the mouse or the bear.
learnerActivities: Children copy the voice and hand position.
Children raise or lower their hands to answer.
Children follow the scarf with their voices and hands.
Child makes a high or a low sound.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the mouse and squeak up high with a hand raised. Show the bear and growl low with a hand lowered. Children: Children copy the voice and hand position.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "High or low?" and make a sound. Children: Children raise or lower their hands to answer.
Step 3. Teacher: Sing "ooh" going up and down with the scarf. Children: Children follow the scarf with their voices and hands.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a turn to be the mouse or the bear. Children: Child makes a high or a low sound.

practical.title: Mouse and bear
steps: Sit in a circle with the two puppets.
Hold up one puppet and sing "ooh".
Children copy the high or low sound together.
practical.safety: Keep voices gentle and stop if a child strains. Give sips of water if voices tire.

differentiation.support: Use one puppet at a time and show with your hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose a puppet and make the sound for others to guess.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the mouse high or low?

expectedOutcomes: Makes a high and a low sound
Uses hands to show high or low
lessons.conclusion: Say goodbye to the mouse in a high voice and the bear in a low voice.
lessons.homeConnection: At home, sing "ooh" up and down and ask your child to copy.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "copy a high voice and a low voice" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Mouse is high, squeak, squeak, squeak. Bear is low, growl, growl, growl.

lessons.title: Week 2 voice check
lessons.subject: Literacy
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child uses loud, quiet, high and low sounds.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can stop and listen for a few seconds and point to the source of a familiar sound.
lessons.starter: Sing the lion and mouse song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes: drum station, puppet station, telephone station.
Ask "Can you play loud?", "Can you whisper?" and "Can you do a high voice?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station and change their sounds on request.
Child shows each sound with a voice or an instrument.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes: drum station, puppet station, telephone station. Children: Children play at each station and change their sounds on request.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Can you play loud?", "Can you whisper?" and "Can you do a high voice?" Children: Child shows each sound with a voice or an instrument.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Voice stations
practical.safety: Supervise instruments and keep volume moderate. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and offer two choices.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to lead a loud and quiet game.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: changes loud and quiet on request; whispers; joins in a voice game.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye in a quiet voice and a big voice.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a loud and quiet game with a cup and spoon at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child uses loud, quiet, high and low sounds" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
